as_told.title: Von Braun's neo-pagan rituals in the German space program

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that in the 1930s and 1940s in Germany, Hermann Oberth, a rocket pioneer, and his student Wernher von Braun, who later led rocket work in America, went through strange neopagan rituals, meaning ceremonies drawn from old pre-Christian religions, as part of the Nazi space programme. In some tellings Michels mentions only von Braun, and once adds that von Braun was believed to be a Freemason, a member of a secretive fraternal society. He tells it to suggest that early space science had a hidden mystical side.
